title: How to use optionsLibrary
text: vignette explains use optionsLibrary package price European options compute Greeks, including simple application. main syntax defined follows: Spot price S0S_0 = S Strike price KK = K Risk-free rate rr = r Dividend yield δ\delta = q Volatility σ\sigma = sigma Time maturity TT = T  Now, load optionsLibrary.

title: How to use optionsLibrary
text: Computing European call:  European put:
code: S <- 100 K <- 100 r <- 0.03 q <- 0 sigma <- 0.2 T <- 0.5 call_price <- bs_price(S, K, r, q, sigma, T, 'call') call_price ## [1] 6.371028 put_price <- bs_price(S, K, r, q, sigma, T, 'put') put_price ## [1] 4.882222

title: How to use optionsLibrary
text: Greeks easily computed similar fashion: Output list form, allowing isolate specific greek:

title: How to use optionsLibrary
code: n <- 100 call_binomial <- binomial_price(S, K, r, q, sigma, T, n, 'call') call_binomial ## [1] 6.35698 put_binomial <- binomial_price(S, K, r, q, sigma, T, n, 'put') put_binomial ## [1] 4.868174

title: How to use optionsLibrary
text: nice application Using optionsLibrary plot convergence binomial price Black-Scholes price:
code: n_steps <- seq(5, 500, by = 5) binomial_prices <- numeric(length(n_steps)) blackscholes_price <- bs_price(S, K, r, q, sigma, T, 'call')  for (i in seq_along(n_steps)) {   n <- n_steps[i]   binomial_prices[i] <- binomial_price(S, K, r, q, sigma, T, n, 'call') } plot(n_steps, binomial_prices, type = 'l', col = '#001c3d', lwd = 2, main = 'Convergence of binomial price', xlab = 'Number of steps (n)', ylab = 'Option price') abline(h = blackscholes_price, col = '#e84e10', lwd = 1.5) legend('topright', legend = c('Binomial price', 'Black-Scholes price'), col = c('#001c3d', '#e84e10'), lty = c(1, 1), lwd = c(3, 3))
